description: An envelope generator that records a contour you draw with the mouse and plays it back down four lanes at different speeds, phases and loop settings, or works as a four-output ADSR

params.text: Fires every lane at once, and in ADSR mode fires a one-shot that reaches sustain and releases without a held gate
Cuts a quiet opening off the recorded gesture, treating anything under 1V for at least 25ms as silence and confirming 12ms of activity before the cut
Cuts the quiet stretch after the last active point off the recorded gesture and adds a return to 0V where one is needed
Steps the selected lane through Off, Forward, Reverse and Ping-Pong looping; in ADSR mode it is a plain on and off
Turns the selected lane's output upside down, so a 0-10V contour comes out running 10V to 0V and a bipolar one changes sign
Sets the playback speed of the selected lane, from 0.05 times to 8 times; in ADSR mode it sets the selected stage's time, or the sustain level
Offsets the selected lane through one whole turn of the gesture; in ADSR mode it bends the selected stage from logarithmic through linear to exponential
Selects which lane the shared speed, phase, loop and invert controls edit; in ADSR mode the four buttons select attack, decay, sustain and release instead
Switches between the recorded-gesture engine and a four-output ADSR envelope, keeping the gesture in the background while ADSR is chosen

inputs.text: A rising edge restarts that voice at the start of the gesture, or at the edge of its loop window; in ADSR mode it fires a one-shot that releases on its own
A rising edge starts a voice and a falling edge glides it down to 0V; in ADSR mode it runs the usual attack, sustain and release
Adds to that lane's phase offset, 10V being one whole turn of the gesture, and the result wraps round
Supplies a tempo for lanes set to a beat division, and never triggers anything; four rising edges establish the beat and only the first channel is read

outputs.text: That lane's envelope, 0-10V unless the menu sets it to 0-5V or bipolar
Carries 10V while that lane or ADSR voice is running
A 1ms pulse at 10V when that lane's one-shot finishes or it crosses the loop boundary its direction defines

notes: it does nothing until a gesture exists: click and hold on the touch strip and move up and down, high on the strip recording 10V and low recording 0V, up to five seconds
starting a new recording stops all playback and replaces the stored gesture when it finishes; the gesture is saved with the patch
with a lane looping, coloured start and end markers appear on the screen and can be dragged to narrow the part of the gesture that plays
clicking the outlined capsule at the top of the screen cycles the selected lane between free running and a quarter, half, one, two or four beats of the clock input
with both the trigger and the gate patched in gesture mode only the trigger is read; in ADSR mode both keep their own jobs
a lane fitted to the clock ignores its speed setting until it is put back to free running
putting a Recollect immediately to the right replaces the played contour with that module's two morphable memories, while recording, triggers and phase stay here
the four per-lane speed CV inputs the manual describes are declared in the code but have no jack on the panel, so nothing can be patched to them
menu: Gesture Mode — chooses the recorded-contour engine, the same choice the panel switch makes
ADSR Mode — chooses the four-output ADSR engine, the same choice the panel switch makes
Gesture trigger behavior — chooses whether a trigger restarts lanes that are already looping or leaves those loops running
Clock fit — sets each lane independently to free running or to a beat division of the clock input
Output voltage ranges — sets each lane's output independently to 0-10V, 0-5V or bipolar, and carries a normalize switch that scales the lane against the gesture's peak
Quantize ADSR Phase CV — is kept so old patches load, and changes nothing in this version because the ADSR contour has no CV path
